question_text: According to the classic sociological research on sentencing cited in the course material, one of three variables in the offender-victim relationship affecting sentence severity for a given crime is the specificity of the victim, which distinguishes crimes against a diffuse victim (the public) from crimes against a:
option_c: Victim located in a foreign country exclusively
option_d: Victim who has already passed away prior to the offense
explanation: One of the three variables affecting sentence severity is the specificity of the victim: whether the victim of an offence is diffuse (the public, as in liquor/gambling violations) or specific (a person or business).

question_text: According to the classic sociological formulation of the inmate social code, cited in the course material, the most inflexible directive concerning loyalty to fellow inmates and betrayal of a fellow captive to institutional officials is expressed as:
explanation: The most inflexible directive of the inmate code, within the category of "don't interfere with inmate interests", is "never rat on a con", with no qualification or mitigating circumstance recognised for betraying a fellow inmate.

question_text: According to the course material's discussion of the inmate code, the maxim "be tough, be a man" falls under the category of rules whose central theme is the maintenance of self, summarized by the directive:
explanation: The category of rules with the central theme of maintaining self, summarized as "don't weaken", includes maxims like "don't whine" and "don't cop out", positively expressed as "be tough; be a man".

question_text: According to the course material, the inmate social system, which centers on the theme of social rejection, is described as most supportive and protective to those inmates who are:
option_b: Least connected to any criminal subculture whatsoever
option_c: Entirely new to the prison environment with no prior exposure
explanation: The inmate social system is most supportive and protective to those inmates who are most criminally acculturated, and conversely most threatening and disruptive to those whose loyalties remain with the non-criminal world.

question_text: According to Gresham Sykes' classic analysis of the "pains of imprisonment", cited in the course material, the five major deprivations suffered by prison inmates are the deprivation of liberty, goods and services, heterosexual relationships, autonomy, and:
option_b: Employment history, in every single case without exception
option_c: Access to reading material of any kind
option_d: The right to a single, specific religion only
explanation: Sykes' classic "pains of imprisonment" framework identifies five major deprivations: liberty, goods and services, heterosexual relationships, autonomy, and security.

question_text: According to the course material's discussion of the deprivation of autonomy, prisoners are subjected to a vast body of rules and commands controlling behavior in minute detail, such as the language used in a letter and the hours of:
explanation: The deprivation of autonomy means prisoners are subjected to rules controlling minute details of behaviour, such as the language used in a letter or the hours of sleeping and eating, removing self-determination.

question_text: According to Donald Clemmer (1950), cited in the course material, "prisonization" is defined as the taking on, in greater or lesser degree, of the folkways, mores, customs, and:
option_b: Formal legal statutes of the surrounding jurisdiction only
option_c: Religious doctrine of the prison chaplain exclusively
option_d: Political affiliations of the prison warden only
explanation: Donald Clemmer (1950) defines prisonization as the taking on, in greater or lesser degree, of the folkways, mores, customs, and general culture of the penitentiary.

question_text: According to the course material's discussion of prisonization, one of the first and most obvious integrative steps a new inmate undergoes concerns his status, in which:
option_b: He is immediately granted early release
option_c: He is exempted from all prison rules for a trial period
option_d: He is given a position of authority over other inmates
explanation: The first and most obvious integrative step of prisonization concerns status: the inmate becomes an anonymous figure in a subordinate group, and a number replaces his name.
